title: Attributing climate-related health burdens in Southeast Asia: a scoping review
abstract: Attributing health outcomes to climate-related exposures is essential for informing adaptive policy, yet Southeast Asia, one of the world's most climate-vulnerable regions, remains critically underrepresented in attribution research. To address this gap, we conducted a scoping review of studies linking climate exposures to health burdens in the region. Although growing evidence demonstrates substantial health impacts from air pollution, heat, and extreme weather, the regional research landscape remains critically imbalanced, marked by neglect of other major hazards-including floods, droughts, extreme rainfall, storms and sea-level rise-and substantial methodological fragmentation. From 5294 records screened, 77 studies met our inclusion criteria. The evidence is dominated by air pollution research, the focus of 70% of studies and linked to up to 31% of all-cause mortality and an estimated 296,000 annual deaths from wildfire smoke during El Niño events. Heat, the second most studied exposure, was associated with up to 8.61% of mortality in Bangkok. In contrast, extreme events such as heatwaves, floods and storms were least frequently investigated. These findings reveal a critical misalignment between regional climate risks and current research focus. Standardized attribution frameworks are urgently needed to support integrated climate-health modeling and guide equitable, evidence-based adaptation across Southeast Asia.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Burden of cardiovascular diseases in the Asia–Pacific region from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050: a secondary analysis of the Global Burden of disease study 2023
abstract: Background: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death globally, with the Asia-Pacific region home to over two-thirds of the world's population, bearing over half of this burden. This study aims to characterise historical trends and forecast CVD burden in the Asia-Pacific from 1990 to 2050, identifying disparities by geographic subregions, sociodemographic index (SDI), and age-sex strata. Methods: Historical (1990-2023) and forecasted (2025-2050) trends in CVD disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) and mortality across 39 Asia-Pacific countries were examined using Global Burden of Disease Study 2023. Findings: In the Asia-Pacific, CVD accounted for 241.2 million DALYs (55.3% of global) in 2023. Crude DALYs rose by 51.3% from 1990 to 2023, despite 36.2% reduction in age-standardised DALYs. Crude DALYs will rise further by 10.7% from 2025 to 2050. Atherosclerotic CVD is the key driver of morbidity, with stroke (1255.0 DALYs per 100,000 population) projected to plausibly surpass ischaemic heart disease (1148.7 DALYs per 100,000 population) by 2050. Disparities in CVD burden exist across SDI (low and low-middle SDI bearing the highest burden), geography (Oceania bearing the highest burden), and age-sex categories (DALYs peaking earlier in males by at least 5 years). Interpretation: The net effect of gains in CVD prevention is offset by the rising crude CVD burden owing to the growing and ageing population. The heterogeneity in CVD burden across countries of different socioeconomic development poses unique challenges in tackling CVD in the Asia-Pacific. Funding: SingHealth Duke-National University of Singapore Cardiovascular Sciences Academic Clinical Programme, the National Medical Research Council of Singapore, and the Stafford Fox Foundation.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Temporal patterns and risk factors of clozapine-associated neutropenia: a nationwide population-based cohort study
abstract: Background: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but neutropenia concerns continue to limit its use. Large real-world evidence on temporal risk patterns, re-initiation, and patient-level determinants remains limited. Methods: We conducted a nationwide cohort study using linked claims and laboratory data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance database (2014-2023). New clozapine users and re-initiators after a ≥42 day interruption were identified. Neutropenia was classified as isolated minor, serious with treatment cessation, or serious without cessation, using absolute neutrophil count thresholds when available and white blood cell counts otherwise. Incidence rates were estimated per 1000 person-years. Temporal changes were examined using joinpoint regression, and risk factors using multivariable cause-specific Cox models with time-varying medication exposures. Findings: Among 12,810 new users, isolated minor neutropenia occurred at 10.5 per 1000 person-years, and serious neutropenia leading to clozapine cessation at 1.7 per 1000 person-years. Joinpoint regression identified early inflection points at week 14 for isolated minor neutropenia, week 15 for serious neutropenia with cessation, and week 6 for serious neutropenia without cessation. Older age and lower baseline white blood cell count were consistently associated with higher risks. Concomitant medication associations were generally stronger for minor than serious events. Re-initiators showed risk patterns comparable to new users, and absolute neutrophil count-based sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. Interpretation: Clozapine-associated neutropenia was uncommon and concentrated early after initiation, with risk stratified by baseline haematological status and age. These findings support risk-informed monitoring strategies. Funding: National Health Research Institutes, Taiwan.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: The impact and evolution of environmental/occupational, behavioural, and metabolic risk factors on CVD burdens in the Asia–Pacific region from 1990 to 2023: a secondary analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstract: Background: Understanding epidemiological trends of the cardiovascular risk factors is integral in designing effective countermeasures in tackling cardiovascular diseases (CVD) in the Asia-Pacific. The study aims to examine the cardiovascular risk factor burden in the Asia-Pacific from 1990 to 2023, stratified by geographic subregion, sociodemographic index, and age-sex strata, to identify the region-specific risk factor targets for CVD prevention. Methods: Estimates from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 were used to quantify cardiovascular mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) attributable to environmental/occupational, behavioural, and metabolic risk factors across 39 Asia-Pacific countries. Findings: In 2023, cardiovascular risk factors contributed to 197.1 million DALYs, with an age-standardised DALY rate of 4463.7 per 100,000 population in the Asia-Pacific, which is 16.4% higher than the global estimate. Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardised DALYs declined by 34.9%, yet crude risk-attributable DALYs rose by 61.5%, as the demographic forces of population ageing (87.3%) and growth (45.3%) overwhelmed the gains from risk exposure reduction (-71.1%). Among risk factor categories, metabolic risk factors contributed to the fastest rise in CVD morbidity (74.3%), followed by behavioural (49.5%), and environmental/occupational risk factors (44.6%). The leading risk factors were high systolic blood pressure, dietary risks, air pollution and high LDL cholesterol. Interpretation: The improvements in cardiovascular risk factor exposure in the Asia-Pacific have been offset by population growth and ageing. The metabolic-centric pattern in risk factors demands for strategies in tackling the region's high priority metabolic risk factor targets. Funding: SingHealth Duke-National University of Singapore Cardiovascular Sciences Academic Clinical Programme, the National Medical Research Council of Singapore, and the Stafford Fox Foundation.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of pumecitinib nasal spray for moderate-to-severe seasonal allergic rhinitis: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial
abstract: Background: Seasonal allergic rhinitis (SAR) is a pollen-triggered condition causing nasal inflammation and quality of life impairment. Pumecitinib, a topical Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor may modulate allergic inflammation. We evaluated the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of pumecitinib nasal spray administered over a 14-day period during the pollen season in patients with moderate-to-severe seasonal allergic rhinitis (SAR). Methods: This phase 2, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study was carried out at 20 centres in China. Adults aged 18-65 years with moderate-to-severe SAR were randomised 1:1:1:1 to receive placebo or pumecitinib nasal spray at doses of 0·2 mg, 1·2 mg, or 2·0 mg administered twice daily for 14 days. The primary efficacy endpoint was the mean change from baseline in daily reflective total nasal symptom score (rTNSS) over 14 days. The secondary endpoints included reflective total ocular symptoms (rTOSS), individual nasal and ocular symptoms, and rhinoconjunctivitis quality of life questionnaire (RQLQ) scores This study is registered with chitr.org.cn, ChiCTR2400081767, and is completed. Findings: Between March 20 and June 5, 2024, 169 patients were randomly assigned and 168 received treatment (92 male, 76 female) and were included in the full analysis set. Both the 1·2 mg and 2·0 mg doses of pumecitinib demonstrated significant improvements compared with placebo in the mean change from baseline in the daily rTNSS over 14 days (least-squares [LS] mean difference -1·2 [95% CI -2·2 to -0·2], p = 0·021, and -1·2 [-2·2 to -0·2], p = 0·018, respectively). These two dosage groups significantly improved rTOSS, individual nasal and ocular symptoms, and RQLQ scores compared to the placebo group. Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) occurred in 15% (0·2 mg), 33% (1·2 mg), 21% (2·0 mg), and 24% (placebo) of patients; most were mild, with no clear dose-response relationship. Interpretation: Pumecitinib 1·2 mg and 2·0 mg twice daily significantly alleviated nasal and ocular symptoms and improved quality of life in moderate-to-severe SAR, with a favourable safety profile during 14-day treatment. This provides proof of concept for topical JAK inhibition in SAR, warranting larger trials. Funding: PrimeGenX Therapeutics Co., Ltd.

title: New Zealand's accelerating smoking decline: the evidence stands
abstract: We welcome the opportunity to respond to the Commentary by Blum and colleagues1 and the Letter by Egger and colleagues2 on our recent paper, New Zealand's accelerating smoking decline: Lessons for tobacco harm reduction.3 To avoid duplication, we address the broader policy and evidence-related issues raised by Blum and colleagues separately from the methodological and interpretive concerns raised by Egger and colleagues.

title: Addressing youth mental health in Southeast Asia: a call to action with a spotlight on Malaysia
abstract: In Malaysia, 1 in 6 children aged 5–15 experience mental health difficulties, with this burden doubling between 2019 and 2023.1 Additionally, approximately 46% of youth report difficulties related to socialisation, including problems playing with others, making or maintaining friendships, or experiences of bullying; and 17% reported emotional difficulties, such as persistent worry, unhappiness, nervousness, clinginess, or being easily frightened. Clinical levels of depression have also been identified in 7.9% of individuals aged 16–19 years and 7.6% of those aged 20–29 years.

title: The landscape of adult obesity in Malaysia: a mapping of evidence and contemporary narrative review
abstract: Malaysia has one of the highest adult overweight/obesity rates (54.4%) regionally, with prevalence projected to keep rising. We mapped and synthesized updated Malaysian adult overweight/obesity research to guide practice and policy. We searched Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar (English, 2016–2024) for studies on adult overweight/obesity in Malaysia. We organized eligible studies into the scopes defined by the national Nutrition Research Priority and conducted thematic narrative synthesis. The evidence base is heavily skewed toward descriptive epidemiology (≈70%), while longitudinal cohorts, experimental designs and health systems research remain scarce. Community-based studies dominate (≈68%), with limited data from clinical or population-based cohorts. Metabolic risk emerges even below BMI 23 kg/m 2 , and waist-to-height ratio >0.5 is a consistent unhealthy threshold. Research on disease burden, economic impact, and long-term outcomes remain limited, constraining policy prioritization. Lifestyle interventions deliver modest effects and are largely confined to micro- and meso-level programmes. Uptake of obesity management medications remains low, bariatric surgery services are expanding but still developing, while policy implementation gaps persist despite existing frameworks. Addressing obesity in Malaysia will require a coordinated, whole-of-society response. Future studies should adopt disease-oriented strategies, harnessing longitudinal national cohorts, pragmatic trials, scalable meso/macro interventions, and a national research collaborative leveraging available resources.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Validation of serological markers of recent exposure to Plasmodium vivax in Cambodia: a longitudinal cohort and cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Asymptomatic Plasmodium vivax infections undermine malaria control by sustaining transmission. This study aimed to validate an eight-marker serological panel (selected from 14 antigens) of P. vivax exposure to detect individuals likely harbouring hypnozoites in rural Cambodia, and to compare it with molecular surveillance for identifying at-risk populations in low-transmission settings. Methods Two studies were conducted in Mondulkiri, Cambodia. In a longitudinal cohort (N = 471), participants were tested monthly for one year for P. vivax using qPCR. At 12 months, IgG responses to 14 antigens were assessed, and Random Forest models (‘Cambodia-specific' and ‘global') were used to classify previous infection, with PCR as the reference standard. In a cross-sectional survey (N = 3538), risk factors for sero- and PCR positivity were assessed using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Findings PCR detected P. vivax in 29.9% (141/471) of participants over the 12-month follow-ups, while 31.8% (150/471) were classified as seropositive at month 12. Of 141 PCR-confirmed cases, 95 were seropositive (67.4%) and 46 seronegative (32.6%) under the 8-antigen panel. The ‘global' model achieved an AUC of 0.81, with 83.3% specificity and 69.5% sensitivity for infections within nine months, increasing to 82% sensitivity for last-month infections. In the cross-sectional study, serology identified more positives than PCR, reflecting detection of exposure not captured by PCR. Interpretation This study provides the first validation of serological markers of P. vivax exposure in Cambodia, showing that such tools can identify recent and asymptomatic infections, though sensitivity was below target. Serology-based surveillance and strategies such as Pv SeroTAT could accelerate malaria elimination. Funding NIH/NIAID, ICEMR Asia-Pacific U19AI129392.

title: Protecting against genetic discrimination requires more than a law
authors: The Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific
abstract: On Oct 8, 2026, Australia will ban life insurance companies nationwide from collecting genetic testing results when reviewing applications. The bill has been widely welcomed by stakeholders, including the Australian Medical Association, the Council of Australian Life Insurers, and the Australian Human Rights Commission. For the many who have hesitated to take a genetic test or participate in genomic research for fear of being refused insurance because of the results, the new law is a significant win against genetic discrimination.

title: Compound climate extremes and “once-in-a-century” risk communication
abstract: In July 2026, China's national meteorological and water resources authorities issued red alerts for flash floods and geological hazards across Liaoning, Jilin, and Anhui provinces, the ceiling of the country's four-level warning system, as the remnant circulation of Typhoon Bavi pushed torrential rain into the northeast, a region not historically associated with typhoon-driven flooding of this scale.1–3 Days earlier, Tropical Storm Maysak had triggered reservoir breaches and large-scale evacuations more than 1500 km to the south, in Guangxi.

title: Completing the referral loop: accountable handovers for social prescribing in Japan
abstract: In my Osaka outpatient practice, I see up to 150 patients a day. People rarely walk in saying they are socially isolated. Instead, they present with insomnia, non-specific symptoms, or requests for medication. Only after multiple consultations does bereavement or the loss of everyday relationships come into focus. These struggles often become visible in the consulting room before they show up in administrative data. For many, returning to a familiar clinic is easier than navigating a social service directly.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Integrated environmental and nutritional efficiencies of local foods in Indonesia: a cradle-to-grave enviro-nutritional life cycle assessment
abstract: Background Indonesia faces simultaneous pressure to improve nutrition and reduce the environmental burden of food systems yet is underrepresented in nutritional life cycle assessment (nLCA) literature. Most existing nutritional functional units (nFUs) were developed in high-income countries, with no consensus on which nFU suits which purpose. Food and Agriculture Organization guidance sets out how such choices should be justified against a study's goal and scope. We evaluated the enviro-nutritional efficiencies of commonly consumed Indonesian foods using a holistic nFU. Methods We modelled 90 Indonesian foods across five food groups (animal-source foods; pulses, nuts, and seeds; starchy staples; vegetables; and fruits) from cradle-to-grave, including home and street preparation, and waste management. LCA results for seven environmental impact categories were integrated with the Nutritional Value Score (NVS), a holistic food rating system capturing nutrient density and protective factors against noncommunicable diseases, using a nFU of 100 NVS. Economic allocation was applied, with cut-off for select co-products. Findings Variability in enviro-nutritional efficiencies reached 211 times the lowest value within food groups. Animal-source foods and vegetables showed the greatest variability across most indicators; pulses, nuts, and seeds and fruits were most variable for water use. Primary production contributed most to environmental impacts for most foods, with exceptions for some processed foods, co-products, and fruits with high refuse. Alignment of enviro-nutritional efficiency with nutritional value was strongest for starchy staples (R 2 = 0.65) and weakest for animal-source foods (R 2 = 0.00). Interpretation Combining holistic nutrient profiling with LCA can identify context-appropriate foods that deliver high nutritional value with lower environmental impact in underrepresented middle-income settings. Findings should be complemented by modelling multi-ingredient foods and sub-national heterogeneity. Funding Nourishing Food Pathways programme.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Landscape of cancer genomics and precision oncology in Japan, South Korea, China, and Australia
abstract: Precision oncology has expanded rapidly across the Asia-Pacific region, yet implementation remains heterogeneous because of differences in health-system organisation, reimbursement, molecular tumour board infrastructure, workforce capacity, and data integration. This structured narrative review with expert consultation compares precision oncology ecosystems in Japan, South Korea, China, and Australia to identify common challenges and implementation strategies across the patient pathway. Although each country has established distinctive genomic medicine programmes, major disparities persist in access to comprehensive genomic profiling, molecularly matched therapies, and longitudinal data infrastructure. Comparative analysis highlights that successful implementation depends not only on sequencing capacity but also on coordinated governance, reimbursement alignment, multidisciplinary decision-making, research integration, and equitable access. Particular attention is required for geographically underserved populations and patients with rare or paediatric cancers. Based on these findings, we propose seven prioritised policy recommendations to strengthen precision oncology implementation, emphasising regional collaboration, interoperable data systems, workforce development, and sustainable reimbursement strategies to improve equity and clinical impact across the Asia-Pacific region.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Family-centred, therapeutic camps for Aboriginal children with complex neurodevelopmental needs and early life trauma in remote Australia: a qualitative study of the Marurra-U family camp
abstract: Background: Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisations in the Fitzroy Valley are internationally recognised for their leadership in supporting children with foetal alcohol spectrum disorder and early life trauma, and their families. This study investigates the design and parent-reported impact of the Marurra-U family camp, a family-centred, therapeutic, recreational camp for Aboriginal children with complex neurodevelopmental or social-emotional needs. Methods: An Aboriginal Participatory Action Approach was used. Nine yarning sessions with 13 Aboriginal parent/carers who attended the Marurra-U family camp in 2024 or 2025 were conducted. Researchers also conducted ethnographic observations whilst participating in the camps. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings: Four themes were constructed: 1) The unique characteristics and design of the Marurra-U family camp, 2) Children actively engaged in camp activities, leading to improved individual, family, and social wellbeing, 3) Parents were motivated and empowered to support their children and communities to thrive, 4) Two-way teams were effective in delivering child and family support. Interpretation: Parents reported that the camps supported emotion regulation, social skills, confidence, and behaviour in children, and empowered, built knowledge, and skills in parents to support their children. This demonstrated that family-centred, therapeutic, recreational camps provide a unique opportunity to support Aboriginal children with complex neurodevelopmental or social-emotional needs. Local leadership, combined with a two-way, trauma-informed, strengths-based approach was key to the success of the family camps. This approach could be adopted by similar communities elsewhere. Funding: This study was supported by a National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia Partnership grant (#APP1171880).
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Trends in Helicobacter pylori prevalence, force of infection, and attributable disease burden in China: a systematic review and Bayesian modelling study
abstract: Background Helicobacter pylori infection is the leading cause of gastric cancer (GC) and peptic ulcer disease (PUD). China has one of the world's largest populations living with H. pylori infection, but long-term age-specific infection dynamics and attributable disease burden remain incompletely characterised. Methods We systematically reviewed studies reporting H . pylori prevalence in China and extracted age-specific prevalence data. We developed a Bayesian catalytic model to jointly synthesise current infection, seropositivity, and ever-infection prevalence, estimating age-specific force of infection (FOI) and prevalence from 1990 to 2023 while accounting for study-level heterogeneity and diagnostic misclassification. Modelled prevalence estimates were combined with published relative risks and national case counts to estimate population attributable fractions (PAFs) and numbers of GC and PUD cases attributable to H . pylori . Findings We included 181 studies in the Bayesian model fitting. Cohorts born after 1980 experienced substantially lower childhood FOI than earlier cohorts, indicating reduced early-life acquisition. However, population prevalence declined only modestly, from 43.1% (95% credible interval 39.1–47.4) in 1990 to 36.3% (33.2–39.6) in 2023. In 2023, estimated PAFs were 70.1% (95% uncertainty interval 51.4–82.4) for non-cardia GC and 49.4% (20.5–70.7) for cardia GC. H . pylori was associated with approximately 340,000–370,000 GC cases and 160,000–210,000 PUD cases, predominantly duodenal ulcers. Interpretation H . pylori prevalence and attributable disease burden remain high in China. Our estimates suggest a more gradual decline than implied by previous studies, supporting consideration of active H. pylori control strategies. Funding China Scholarship Council, EU4Health.

title: Corrigendum to “HPV vaccination policies and implementation for adolescents in low- and middle-income countries: a scoping review” [The Lancet Regional Health-Western Pacific Volume 72, July (2026), 101919]
abstract: The authors regret that the published version of “Fig. 3. Trends in HPV vaccination coverage by age 15, grouped by delivery platform (2011–2024)” contained an error. Fig. 3 combines coverage trend panels for four indicators-15HPVC_F, 15HPV1_M, 15HPVC_M, and 15HPV1_F. Due to an error during figure preparation, the panels intended to show 15HPVC_F, 15HPV1_M, and 15HPVC_M were all mistakenly replaced with the panel for 15HPV1_F. The corrected Fig. 3 is provided with this corrigendum. All other results, tables, and text in the article remain unchanged.

title: Irritable bowel syndrome and suicide risk among adolescents: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Background: Adolescent suicide is a global public health concern. Emerging evidence from the gut-brain axis and interoception framework suggests links between functional gastrointestinal disorders, visceral bodily signals, and mental health vulnerability. However, evidence on the association between irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and adolescent suicidality remains scant. This study aimed to examine the longitudinal associations of IBS with suicide risk and attempts among Chinese adolescents. Methods: Data were drawn from a school-based prospective cohort study with citywide census-style recruitment in Southern China. IBS, demographic, behavioural, and emotional symptom measures were assessed, along with two suicidality outcomes: overall suicide risk and past-12-month suicide attempts as a behavioural indicator. Mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between baseline IBS and follow-up suicidality. Subgroup analyses (sex, age group, residential area, only-child status, and subjective SES) tested the robustness of these associations. Alternative indirect pathways linking IBS, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and suicidality outcomes were examined. Findings: = 1.99). IBS prevalence was 7.0% (n = 6435). Suicide risk and suicide attempts had incidence rates of 6.1% (n = 4454) and 3.5% (n = 3035), respectively. IBS was prospectively associated with increased suicide risk (OR [95% CI] = 2.33 [2.18, 2.49], p < 0.0001) and attempts (OR [95% CI] = 2.17 [1.93, 2.44], p < 0.0001). These associations remained significant after adjustment for demographic, behavioural, emotional symptom, and baseline suicidality covariates (suicide risk: aOR [95% CI] = 1.27 [1.18, 1.37], p < 0.0001; suicide attempts: aOR [95% CI] = 1.21 [1.06, 1.38], p = 0.0060). Depressive and anxiety symptoms partially mediated these associations. Interpretation: IBS was prospectively associated with adolescents' elevated risk of suicidality. IBS may serve as a meaningful marker of suicide risk, potentially reflecting altered gut-brain and interoceptive processes, and underscoring the need to integrate mental health screening with gastrointestinal care for early suicide identification and prevention. Funding: Research fund of Vanke School of Public Health, Tsinghua University.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Change in the life expectancy gap among people with mental illness: a 14-year population-based cohort study in Australia
abstract: Background: People with psychiatric disorders die substantially earlier than the general population, with life expectancy gaps of 10-20 years reported internationally. Prior Australian data indicated this gap was widening, whereas evidence from other countries has been mixed. We aimed to determine whether the life expectancy gap in people with hospitalised psychiatric disorders versus the general population is changing in Queensland, Australia, and to identify which causes of death drive excess mortality. Methods: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using linked Queensland hospital admissions and death registry data. Adults (≥18 years) with a principal psychiatric diagnosis across seven diagnostic categories were included, excluding dementia. Life expectancy was estimated using life-table methods and compared to Queensland norms. We calculated standardised mortality ratios (SMRs) across four time-periods and quantified the absolute and proportional contribution of specific causes to excess mortality using excess mortality rates per 100,000 person-years and attributable fractions. Findings: The analytic cohort comprised 255,448 individuals contributing 2,204,719 person-years. The life expectancy gap narrowed significantly for both sexes (p < 0·001): from 13·4 to 9·4 years in females and 16·7 to 12·1 years in males. All-cause SMRs declined from 2·35 (95% CI 2·23-2·47) to 1·73 (1·67-1·79) in females and 3·12 (2·98-3·25) to 2·10 (2·04-2·16) in males. The gap did not narrow significantly in either sex among people with schizophrenia or other psychoses, in females with affective psychoses, or in females with neurotic or alcohol and substance use disorders. Although intentional self-harm was the largest single contributor to proportional excess mortality in males, the combined excess mortality rate from physical health causes was substantially greater than from self-harm (440·0 and 441·9 versus 163·7 and 83·5 per 100,000 person-years in males and females respectively). Interpretation: The life expectancy gap between people with psychiatric disorders and the general population in Queensland has narrowed over 14 years, although the absolute gap remains considerable, and people with schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders have not shared equally in these gains. Physical illness is the principal driver of excess mortality, therefore prioritising physical health care for people with mental illness is essential to closing the gap, especially in psychotic disorders. Funding: None.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Outcomes of a state-wide virtual emergency department in Victoria, Australia: a linked data analysis of emergency department utilisation and hospital use
abstract: Background: The Victorian Virtual Emergency Department (VVED) is a synchronous video-based emergency care service established to reduce the burden on physical EDs by managing patients remotely. Despite rapid growth in virtual emergency care models, evidence regarding downstream hospital utilisation and factors associated with subsequent ED presentation remains limited. We aimed to examine downstream ED utilisation following a VVED consultation and identify factors associated with unplanned ED presentation. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using linked statewide administrative data. The study included all patients registered with the VVED between 1 July 2022 and 23 June 2023. The primary outcome was unplanned ED presentation within 48 h among patients initially managed in the community. Secondary outcomes included discharge destination and planned and unplanned ED utilisation within 48 h and 7 days. Mixed-effects logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with unplanned ED presentation. Findings: Of 100,422 VVED presentations, 75.5% (n = 75,871) were managed at home and 15.3% (n = 15,353) were referred to a physical ED. Among patients managed at home, 8.2% (n = 6202) attended a physical ED within 48 h, increasing to 11.4% (n = 8667) within 7 days. Overall, 81.5% (n = 81,840) of patients did not attend a physical ED within 48 h. Primary diagnosis category was the only factor independently associated with unplanned ED presentation within 48 h. Interpretation: Most patients were managed in the community, with low unplanned ED utilisation. Higher unplanned rates in our Healthcare Professional pathway likely reflect greater clinical complexity. Further research is needed to explore long-term outcomes, patient perspectives, optimal referral pathways for high-risk groups and the temporal and causal relationship between VVED implementation and physical ED utilisation. Funding: This study was conducted as part of a Digital Health Cooperative Research Centre project, a partnership between La Trobe University, Northern Health, and the Victorian Department of Health.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: A landscape of metabolic burden and its cardiovascular impact across the adult lifespan: a prospective cohort study of 7.5 million people in Northwestern China
abstract: Background: Metabolic abnormalities are increasingly prevalent in young adults and commonly cluster in the elderly. We aimed to map the landscape of metabolic burden and quantify the related cardiovascular impact across the adulthood in Chinese population. Methods: The prospective cohort included 7,513,828 adults (3,907,602 women and 3,606,226 men) from northwestern China who were free of cardiovascular disease (CVD) at baseline. Participants were grouped by age (18-<40, 40-<60, 60-<80, and ≥80 years). Age-specific distribution and time-series trajectories were depicted for 6 major metabolic risk factors, including obesity, hepatic steatosis, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, and renal dysfunction. Their age-specific associations with incident CVD and population attributable fractions (PAFs) were assessed, considering potential sex difference. Findings: Metabolic states exhibited obvious age-dependent sexual dimorphism, characterized by an initial female advantage in young adults which reversed around age 45. Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, the metabolic factors exhibited strong associations with incident CVD in younger adults which gradually attenuated with advancing age. In particular, the HR for hypertension declined from 3.60 in the youngest group to 2.12 in the middle-aged group, 1.41 in the older group, and 1.21 in the very old (≥80 years). Regardless of age or sex, obesity demonstrated the highest PAF to CVD. For combined metabolic burden, the PAF was highest in middle-aged group (37.89%), followed by people aged 18-<40 years (29.78%) and 60-<80 years (25.24%), and lowest in the very old (15.85%). The PAF was higher in men than women only in those under 40 and the sex disparity reversed in the older groups. Among metabolically abnormal participants, transitioning to a healthier metabolic state, within an average of 1 year, was associated with a substantially reduced risk of CVD, particularly in the younger groups. Interpretation: The metabolic burden and its cardiovascular effects are heterogeneous across demographic segments, supporting the rationale of implementing age-specific and gender-sensitive strategies for metabolic management and CVD prevention. Funding: Key Research and Development Project of Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region; Suzhou Applied Basic Research (Medical and Health) Science and Technology Innovation Project; Jiangsu Frontier Technology Research and Development Program.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Quantitative refinement and multicentre psychometric validation of the Chinese total knee arthroplasty patient-reported outcome measure: a prospective cohort study with repeated measures
abstract: Background: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) requires valid, culturally appropriate patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). A 35-item preliminary Chinese Total Knee Arthroplasty Patient-reported Outcome Measurement (CTP) was previously developed by our group through qualitative research with Chinese patients and multidisciplinary experts, but it had not undergone quantitative refinement or prospective multicentre psychometric validation. The present study aimed to refine the instrument and evaluate the psychometric properties of its operated-knee core score. Methods: We conducted a prospective multicentre cohort psychometric study with repeated assessments at tertiary hospitals in Xi'an, Chengdu, and Lanzhou. Participants were recruited from June 2023 to June 2024, with 12-month follow-up continuing through June 2025. Three independent cohorts were used for quantitative item screening, final scale construction, and psychometric evaluation. We assessed internal consistency (Cronbach's α), test-retest reliability (ICC), structural validity, convergent validity (correlations with WOMAC), and responsiveness (effect size [ES]; standardised response mean [SRM]). Findings: The three analytic cohorts included 321, 529, and 898 participants, respectively (total n = 1748). Across the three cohorts, the mean age was 66·5 years (SD 7·2), and 1195 participants (68·4%) were female. Exploratory factor analysis supported a three-factor structure (Function, Symptoms, Quality of Life) explaining 72·2% of variance, with all item loadings ≥0·40. The final clinical questionnaire contained 22 items. The principal psychometric analyses evaluated a 16-item operated-knee core score, which showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0·864) and good test-retest reliability (ICC = 0·836). Convergent validity was supported by a strong correlation between CTP Function and WOMAC Function (r = 0·698; 95% CI 0·663-0·730; p < 0·001). At 12 months, the mean operated-knee core score decreased from 33·52 (SD 8·74) to 21·81 (SD 9·81), with an ES of 1·34 and an SRM of 1·66. Interpretation: The final CTP is a 22-item, target-population-informed clinical PROM. Its 16-item operated-knee core score showed satisfactory reliability and responsiveness, with partial support for the proposed three-factor structure and convergent validity for selected overlapping constructs. Funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China, Key Research and Development Program of Shaanxi Province, Cultivation Project for General Project of Xi'an Health Commission, Xi'an Municipal Science and Technology Plan Project: General Medical Research Project, the Program for Innovation Team of Shaanxi Province.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: HBsAg seroclearance with HBV DNA <100 IU/mL and long-term risks of adverse liver events, all-cause mortality, and cause-specific mortality in chronic hepatitis B: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Background: Sustained HBsAg seroclearance with HBV DNA suppression is associated with favorable outcomes in chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but its associations with overall survival and cause-specific mortality remain insufficiently quantified. Methods: In a prospective, multicenter, community-based cohort of 6018 Chinese CHB patients, sustained HBsAg seroclearance with HBV DNA <100 IU/mL was modeled as a time-dependent exposure using propensity score-matched Cox regression. We estimated population attributable fractions (PAFs) for burden associated with persistent infection and restricted mean survival time (RMST) for survival difference. Findings: During a median 11.1-year follow-up, 1029 participants with sustained HBsAg seroclearance and HBV DNA <100 IU/mL (97.0% spontaneously) were compared with 2931 matched participants with persistent infection. This serovirological state was associated with lower risks of cirrhosis (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.45; 95% CI, 0.27-0.74) and hepatocellular carcinoma (aHR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.33-0.81). It was also associated with lower all-cause mortality (aHR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.36-0.60), as well as liver-related, extrahepatic cancer-related, and cardiovascular mortality. The RMST difference was 5.17 years within the observed age range. Interpretation: Sustained HBsAg seroclearance accompanied by very low HBV DNA levels was associated with lower risks of adverse liver outcomes and selected extrahepatic mortality, as well as longer RMST, highlighting the prognostic relevance of this serovirological state for long-term risk stratification in CHB. Funding: National Natural Science Foundation of China (82373654, 82674792); Jiangsu Provincial Key Discipline of Epidemiology (ZDXK202250); Scientific Research Project of Jiangsu Provincial Health Commission (H2023041); Science and Technology Plan Project of Jiangsu Provincial Disease Control and Prevention Administration (JSJK2026M00015).

title: The epidemiological impact and effectiveness of herpes zoster vaccination among older and pharmacologically immunocompromised adults: a population-based observational study
abstract: Background: Australia used the live attenuated herpes zoster vaccine (ZVL, Zostavax®) for 70-79 year-old adults in its National Immunisation Program from 2016. In November 2023 this was replaced with the recombinant adjuvanted herpes zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) and eligibility expanded to include adults ≥65 years old and immunocompromised adults ≥18 years. We aimed to assess the vaccine program impact and RZV effectiveness in eligible adults. Methods: Using linked national immunisation registry and zoster-specific antiviral prescription data as a proxy outcome, patterns of antiviral use from 2014 to 2025 were assessed in an ecological study. A separate vaccine effectiveness (VE) study estimated VE using multivariable Cox-regression hazards models with time-varying vaccine exposure in 4,488,937 individuals aged ≥65 years (65+ cohort) and 239,002 adults aged ≥18 years who were immunocompromised due to medication use (pharmacologically immunocompromised cohort). VE was estimated using the formula VE = (1-hazard ratio) × 100%. Findings: Declines in zoster-specific antiviral prescriptions temporally coincided with vaccine program changes between 2014 and 2025. During November 2023-June 2025, herpes zoster incidence in the 65+ years and the pharmacologically immunocompromised cohorts were 9.99 and 17.59 per 1000 person-years respectively. By 30th June 2025, 35% (N = 1,569,950) of the 65+ cohort and 22% (N = 51,455) of the pharmacologically immunocompromised cohort had received 2 doses of RZV. Comparing 2 doses of RZV to those not vaccinated in the 65+ years cohort, 2 dose VE was 63% (95% CI: 62%, 64%), with similar estimates across age groups (65-69, 70-79, and 80+ years). Among the pharmacologically immunocompromised adults VE was 43% (95% CI: 38%, 49%). Interpretation: RZV demonstrated good protection against zoster in older adults, with lower effectiveness in the pharmacologically immunocompromised population. Vaccine uptake in both cohorts was suboptimal. Improving vaccine coverage and ongoing evaluation of effectiveness over extended durations is needed, particularly in the immunocompromised population. Funding: This work was funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Projections of diabetes mellitus in Japan through 2040: a bayesian age-period-cohort analysis of the national health and nutrition survey population
abstract: Background: Accurate projection of the burden of diabetes mellitus (DM) requires consideration of age, period, and cohort (APC) effects underlying prevalence trends. We estimated projected trends in DM prevalence and case numbers in Japan from 2020 until 2040, by sex, using the Bayesian APC (BAPC) model. Methods: We employed Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling and prediction (BAMP), using observed populations (aged 40 years or older) and DM cases from the National Health and Nutrition Survey from 2003 to 2019, to project national-level DM prevalence and cases from 2020 to 2040 using the national-level projected population until 2040. We further compared BAPC's predictive performance with that of conventional prediction model 1 with a constant prevalence rate and conventional prediction model 2 with a monotonically changing prevalence rate, using root mean square error (RMSE) between observed and projected case numbers for model validation during 2015-2019. Findings: The prevalence (95% credible intervals) of DM in Japan was projected to increase from 16.4% (12.3%-21.6%) in 2020 to 18.1% (6.4%-40.8%) in 2040 in men by BAPC, while it was projected to decline from 9.6% (6.8%-13.3%) to 7.7% (2.3%-22.7%) in women, variations primarily suggested by age effects and cohort effects. DM cases (95% credible intervals) are expected to increase from 6,070,000 (4,530,000-7,980,000) in 2020 to 6,336,000 (2,230,000-14,290,000) in 2040 in men, while they were expected to decline from 3,995,000 (2,840,000-5,540,000) to 3,032,000 (910,000-8,910,000) in women. The BAPC demonstrated the best predictive performance with lower RMSE (men, 40.1; women, 11.5), compared to conventional model 1 (men, 51.3; women, 20.8) and conventional model 2 (men, 42.4; women, 23.1). Interpretation: This study suggests that Japan is expected to experience increases in the prevalence and number of DM cases from 2020 to 2040, particularly among men, given the APC factors. Funding: This research was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Reimagining healthcare in Indonesia for 2045: a Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific Commission
abstract: In 2045, Indonesia will mark a century of independence. Home to about 3.6% of the world's population,1 Indonesia is the world's largest archipelagic state and home to the most populous island on Earth. Almost 290 million people are spread across approximately 6000 inhabited islands, with historically unique languages, ethnicities and cultures.2 The result is a country of extraordinary geographic, ethnic, linguistic, and cultural diversity. The country's burden of disease is also not shared evenly.

title: Optimising a digital parent-based intervention to improve adolescent health risk behaviours in families living in socio-economically disadvantaged communities: findings from the Health4Life Parents & Teens factorial randomised trial
abstract: Background: Adolescence is a critical period when health risk behaviours contributing to long-term disease burden emerge. Parent-based interventions show promise, yet engagement is often low and few exist for socioeconomically disadvantaged communities. We applied the Multiphase Optimisation Strategy (MOST) to identify a maximally effective, minimally burdensome digital intervention to support parents to improve adolescent health risk behaviours. Methods: A 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 factorial randomised trial was conducted with parents of adolescents (aged 11-15 years), living in a disadvantaged area of New South Wales, Australia (quintiles 1-2, Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage). Participants were recruited via social media and in community settings and randomised to 1 of 16 experimental conditions via a Blockrand-generated scheme in R. All participants received access to six online modules targeting key health risk behaviours (core component). Four components were experimentally tested (present vs absent): text messages, tailored feedback, stress management training, and telehealth coaching, resulting in 16 possible intervention combinations. Participants and researchers were not masked to allocation. The primary outcome was 3-month change in parental encouragement of adolescent health habits (Health Habits subscale of Parenting to Reduce Adolescent Depression Anxiety Scale; possible range 0-12). Parent-reported perceived effort of completing each component was examined (5-point scale: 'no effort at all' to 'huge effort'). The trial was prospectively registered (ACTRN12624001492549; 20/12/2024). Findings: = 0.31, p = 0.0051, mean difference = 0.62, 95% CI = 0.19 to 1.04, Cohen's d = 0.38) improved parental encouragement, while text messages had a negative effect (B = -0.33, p < 0.0026, mean difference = -0.66, 95% CI = -1.09 to -0.23, Cohen's d = -0.41). Telehealth coaching yielded the greatest improvements, but highest perceived effort (mean = 2.4/5, SD = 1.2). Tailored feedback achieved comparable gains, with significantly lower effort (mean = 2.1/5, SD = 1.0; p = 0.03). The optimised intervention comprised online modules and tailored feedback. No adverse events were reported. Interpretation: Using a highly efficient MOST factorial design, we identified a low-burden, highly scalable intervention for parents living in disadvantaged communities, ready for evaluation in a definitive randomised controlled trial. Funding: Medical Research Future Fund (2021535).
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Trends and disparities in hepatitis B burden in the Western Pacific Region, 2015–2024: a subregional analysis using modelled data
abstract: Background: The Western Pacific Region (WPR) carries one of the world's largest hepatitis B virus (HBV) burdens, but elimination progress remains uneven. We assessed changes in HBV burden and heterogeneity in elimination progress across the WPR during 2015-2024. Methods: We conducted a regional ecological study using standardised modelled estimates from the Center for Disease Analysis Foundation for 34 WPR countries and areas from 2015 to 2024. Country-specific temporal trends were quantified using log-linear regression to estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) with 95% CIs. We assessed incidence-mortality divergence, differences in EAPCs across analytical subregions, associations between vaccination coverage and HBV burden, and sensitivity to influential observations, shared model trajectories, non-linearity, and alternative country classification. Findings: Regional HBV prevalence declined from 5.28% (95% UI 4.23-6.34) in 2015 to 4.58% (3.66-5.49) in 2024, and chronic HBV incidence declined from 6.32 to 3.16 per 100,000 population. Under-five prevalence plateaued at approximately 0.28-0.29% from 2019, remaining above the WHO 2030 target of ≤0.1%. Crude modelled HBV mortality increased from 22.88 to 24.70 per 100,000. Of 34 countries and areas, 55.9% had declining chronic incidence alongside increasing mortality. Incidence and mortality EAPCs were modestly correlated (r = 0.39, 95% CI 0.06-0.64; p = 0.023), while evidence of systematic differences across analytical subregions was limited. Interpretation: Declining HBV incidence has not been accompanied by declining mortality in many WPR countries and areas. Elimination monitoring should therefore assess transmission and mortality as distinct outcomes and account for substantial country-level heterogeneity. Funding: World Health Organization.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Trends and transition dynamics of heated tobacco product use in Japan, 2015–2025: a repeated cross-sectional and longitudinal study
abstract: Background: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) diffused rapidly in Japan, but transition dynamics remain unclear. We examined trends in HTP use and routes underlying its growth. Methods: Using data from the Japan Society and New Tobacco Internet Survey, 2015-2025, we estimated weighted prevalence of HTP use (N = 161,583). Sex- and age-standardised prevalence was used to estimate segmented trends with a 2018 knot. Among respondents observed in consecutive years (93,540 pairs), we fitted a multinomial transition model across five states (Never, Non-current, Cigarette-only, HTP-only, and Dual use) and decomposed changes in standardised HTP prevalence into four categories: uptake from Never/Non-current states, switching from Cigarette-only to HTP, switching back to Cigarette-only, and exit to Non-current use. Findings: Weighted HTP prevalence increased from 0.1% to 14.9% during 2015-2025. Standardised prevalence rose sharply through 2018 (3.33 percentage points/year) and more gradually thereafter (0.92 percentage points/year). Transition probabilities showed post-2018 persistence of HTP-only/Dual use (67.9% and 57.0%, respectively). In the longitudinal decomposition, mean annual entry into HTP use increased from 2.16 percentage points before 2018 to 3.48 after 2018, while mean annual exit changed from -0.39 to -2.30. After 2018, entry from Non-current states increased markedly, whereas contributions from Never states were smaller and switching from Cigarette-only to HTP remained substantial. Interpretation: HTP use in Japan shifted around 2018 from rapid expansion to slower but sustained growth. Within the transition-eligible sample, later growth reflected multiple dynamics-including continued cigarette-to-HTP switching, persistence within HTP-using states, and increasing uptake from Non-current states-rather than cigarette substitution alone. Funding: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science KAKENHI (25H01079).

title: Clean air for a healthier Western Pacific region
authors: The Lancet Regional Health – Western Pacific
abstract: Clean air is not a privilege, but a prerequisite for health and human rights. Recognising this, the UN General Assembly designated Sept 7 as International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies, calling attention to the need for stronger action on air pollution.

title: Effect of statins on the mortality of long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a population-based study in endemic area
abstract: Background Long-term survivors of nasopharyngeal cancer (NPC) are at risk of excessive mortality. This territory-wide cohort study aims to investigate the relationship between statin use and mortality among 5-year survivors of NPC. Methods This is a retrospective cohort study conducted with data from a territory-wide registry. Patients who survived five years after being diagnosed with non-metastatic NPC in Hong Kong between 1 January 1997 and 30 December 2015 were included. Patients were divided into statin users and statin non-users. We performed the inverse propensity of treatment weighting (IPTW) method to balance confounding factors. The primary outcome of overall survival (OS) was compared between the two groups and stratified by the cause of death, statin types and duration of statin usage. Findings 7872 subjects (2439 statin users and 5433 statin non-users) were included in the final analysis. The 10-year, 15-year, and 20-year survival probabilities of statin users compared to non-users were 89.1 vs. 71.8%, 77.2 vs. 55.1%, and 59.2 vs. 42.4% respectively (HR 0.46, p < 0.001). After adjusting for immortal time bias, the hazard ratio for overall survival was 0.71 ( p < 0.001). Statin use was associated with reduced risk of death due to secondary malignancy (HR 0.51; p = 0.002), cardiovascular disease (HR 0.64; p = 0.002), and pulmonary disease (HR 0.64; p = 0.011). Mortality was significantly lower in long-term statin usage of >6 years (HR 0.31; p < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, patients who received second- or third-generation statins were associated with a lower risk of mortality (HR 0.66 and HR 0.41, respectively), although this finding requires further validation. Interpretation Our study suggests that statin usage is associated with reduced mortality in long-term NPC survivors. Further prospective study is warranted. Funding This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Burden of typhoid fever in primary and hospital care in Indonesia: a serial cross-sectional study using national health insurance (BPJS Kesehatan) data, 2015–2023
abstract: Background: Despite Indonesia's high typhoid burden, subnational prevalence data remain sparse, limiting risk mapping and targeted interventions. We characterised trends in typhoid presentation in primary care and hospital settings, described geographic patterns, and identified factors associated with hospitalisation. Methods: national insurance sample. Typhoid fever cases were identified using ICD-10 codes A01.0-A01.09, with sampling weights applied to generate nationally representative estimates. Temporal trends were assessed using time-series analyses, and factors associated with hospitalisation using Poisson regression. Findings: From 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2023, an estimated 8,180,668 ICD-10 coded typhoid-related healthcare visits were recorded, including 3,895,695 hospital admissions. Mean annual prevalence peaked at 314 per 100,000 in hospitals (2016) and 347 per 100,000 in primary care (2017), with the highest prevalence among children younger than 5 years. Cases were concentrated on Java. Higher proportion of hospitalisation was observed among BPJS Kesehatan-subsidised participants (aPR 1·07; 95% CI: 1·05-1·09), elderly aged ≥65 years (aPR 1·07; 95% CI: 1·04-1·09), and children (0-5 years: aPR 1·02; 95% CI: 1·01-1·03; 6-18 years: aPR 1·03; 95% CI: 1·02-1·04). Interpretation: Typhoid fever remains a substantial public health burden in Indonesia despite a declining trend. Higher hospitalisation among subsidised participants and vulnerable age groups reflects persistent socioeconomic and age-related inequities. Control efforts should integrate water and sanitation improvements and vaccination, informed by epidemiological patterns to optimise geographic targeting and dose scheduling. Funding: Gates Foundation.

title: Tirofiban vs standard antiplatelet therapy in acute branch atheromatous disease-related stroke: a multicenter, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint, parallel-group, phase III clinical trial
abstract: Background: Tirofiban is sometimes used empirically for branch atheromatous disease (BAD)-related stroke, but its benefit in this population remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of intravenous tirofiban administered within 48 h of onset in patients with acute BAD-related stroke. Methods: This multicentre, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint clinical trial enrolled patients with BAD-related stroke within 48 h of onset from 25 hospitals in China between 9 November 2023 and 22 November 2025. Eligible patients were randomly assigned to the tirofiban group (intravenously, 0.4 μg/kg per minute for 30 min, followed by a 0.1 μg/kg per minute for 47.5 h) or standard antiplatelet therapy group (oral aspirin with or without clopidogrel) for 48 h. The primary endpoint was an excellent functional outcome, defined as a score of 0 or 1 on the modified Rankin Scale at 90 days. Safety outcomes included major bleeding within 90 days. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06037889). Findings: Among 516 patients randomized, 513 were included in the primary analysis (258 with tirofiban and 255 with standard antiplatelet therapy). An excellent functional outcome was observed in 181 of 258 patients (70.2%) in the tirofiban group and 178 of 255 (69.8%) in the standard antiplatelet therapy group (risk ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.90-1.13]; P = 0.93). Major bleeding occurred in 0 of 259 participants in the tirofiban-exposed safety population and 1 of 245 (0.4%) in the standard-antiplatelet-exposed safety population. Interpretation: Among patients with acute BAD-related stroke, intravenous tirofiban administered within 48 h of onset without concomitant oral antiplatelet therapy was not superior to standard antiplatelet therapy for achieving an excellent functional outcome at 90 days. These findings should not be extrapolated to substantially earlier treatment or to other tirofiban-based antiplatelet strategies. Funding: National High Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding, Capital's Funds for Health Improvement and Research, CAMS Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences (CIFMS), Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, and China Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Company (CSPC) NBP Pharmaceurical Co., Ltd.

title: When global climate diplomacy comes to the Pacific, health must be at the table
abstract: This month, global climate diplomacy will come to the Pacific. With Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia co-hosting the UNFCCC Pre-COP ahead of COP31 in Nadi and Funafuti,1 the international community will gather in a region where the impacts of climate change are a daily and lived reality.

title: “Indigenous models of social prescribing”–a six-domain framework for social wellbeing and other support services delivered by Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Organisations
abstract: This viewpoint examines the literature to illuminate the role of Aboriginal community-controlled health organisations in supporting access to social wellbeing and other support services that address the social and cultural determinants of health and wellbeing for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. Our papers call on primary care providers, researchers, and policymakers to apply and test the six-domain framework we developed to describe their engagement with social wellbeing and other support services, and to showcase their work, control, and financial needs.

title: A multidomain, nurse-led, mobile health-supported intervention for dementia risk reduction in primary care (HAPPI MIND): a pragmatic, single-blind, two-arm, cluster randomised controlled trial
abstract: Background: Modifiable midlife risk factors contribute substantially to dementia, yet scalable preventive interventions in primary care are limited. We evaluated the effectiveness of a multidomain, nurse-led, mobile health (mHealth)-supported behavioural intervention (HAPPI MIND) among middle-aged adults. Methods: We conducted a cluster randomised controlled trial in adults aged 45-65 years with ≥2 modifiable dementia risk factors, from 31 Australian general practices (intervention = 13, control = 18). Clinics were randomised to the intervention or control group. Practice nurses collected socio-demographic and clinical data using validated tools. Participants completed the Australian National University-Alzheimer's Disease Risk Index (ANU-ADRI) dementia risk assessment, which assessed exposure to modifiable risks and protective factors for dementia. Intervention participants received five nurse-led motivational interviewing sessions over 12 months, an individualised action plan, and access to the mHealth application. Control participants received the ANU-ADRI report, an educational booklet on dementia risk reduction, and referral to their general practitioner as appropriate. Outcome assessors and data analysts were blinded. The primary outcome was the change in ANU-ADRI score from baseline to 12 months. Analyses followed intention-to-treat principles using linear mixed-effects models with multiple imputation for missing data. The trial was prospectively registered (ACTRN12621001168842); the intervention is complete, and this report presents the prespecified primary outcome at 12 months. Findings: Between February 2022 and April 2023, 403 participants (intervention = 201; control = 202) were enrolled (mean age 56.4 years [SD 5.7]; 63% female). At 12 months, the adjusted mean change in ANU-ADRI score was 0.791 (95% CI -0.895 to 2.478) in the intervention group and -0.807 (-2.339 to 0.725) in the control group, with an adjusted between-group mean difference of 1.598 (0.423-2.773; p = 0.0080), favouring the intervention. Results from per-protocol and complete-case analyses were consistent. Seven adverse events occurred, including two deaths (one in each group). Interpretation: A multidomain, nurse-led, mHealth-supported behavioural intervention produced modest but statistically significant improvements in estimated dementia risk profiles over 12 months among middle-aged adults in Australian primary care. Further implementation, processes, and economic evaluations are needed before broader adoption can be recommended. Funding: Australian Government National Health and Medical Research Council, Boosting Dementia Research Grants (GNT1171851).
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: Implementation of the National Asthma Guidelines in New Zealand: a retrospective patient-level study of the change to anti-inflammatory reliever therapy in 324,972 patients
abstract: Background: The updated New Zealand asthma guidelines in 2020, aligning with global asthma guideline recommendations, advocated for a fundamental shift from short-acting β2-agonist (SABA) reliever therapy to anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR) therapy (ICS-formoterol) in adults and adolescents. While aggregate population-level data indicate increased ICS-formoterol dispensings, patient-level changes in medication use remain unclear. We examined medication use patterns to assess early practice changes across the entire asthma population. Methods: We conducted a retrospective study using the New Zealand national linked health datasets. Patients aged ≥12 with asthma were identified from hospitalisation and/or dispensing data, and categorised by the complete set of inhaler classes dispensed in the three months preceding their final dispensing date within the baseline (July 2018-June 2020) and post-guideline (June 2020-June 2022) periods. Nine mutually exclusive categories were defined without applying any hierarchy between medications: SABA only; ICS, non-formoterol ICS-LABA, and ICS-formoterol, each with and without a concurrently dispensed SABA; other regimens; and no inhaled medication. Age subgroups (12-44 and ≥ 45 years) were examined. Children aged < 12 years throughout follow-up, who were outside the scope of the recommendation, served as a comparison cohort for difference-in-differences estimation. Findings: The cohort included 324,972 patients aged ≥12 years. At baseline, the SABA-only group was the most common (30.5%). Post-guideline, dispensing of the guideline-recommended regimen, ICS-formoterol without SABA, more than doubled from 10.9% to 23.8%, and any ICS-formoterol use rose from 18.9% to 34.5%. The proportion of patients dispensed any SABA fell from 74.1% to 60.8%. Of patients dispensed SABA only pre-guideline, 57.1% were dispensed SABA only again, while 17.6% changed to ICS-formoterol without SABA and 8.1% to ICS-formoterol with SABA. Continuity was high among patients on maintenance therapy (55.9% for ICS, 74.3% for non-formoterol ICS-LABA) and among those already dispensed ICS-formoterol (89.0%). Among post-guideline ICS-formoterol users, 31.1% were also dispensed a SABA, compared with 63.8% of non-formoterol ICS-LABA users and 70.2% of ICS users. Using children aged < 12 years as a comparison cohort, difference-in-differences estimates were +8.4 percentage points for ICS-formoterol without SABA and -8.3 percentage points for total SABA supply, but -0.2 percentage points for SABA monotherapy. Interpretation: The impact of the guideline change was substantial but selective. While the update facilitated transition for patients already receiving maintenance therapy, most patients on SABA-only regimens did not switch to the preferred AIR regimen. Further targeted implementation strategies beyond guideline publication are required to address this gap and ensure evidence-based care is consistently delivered. Funding: None.
journal_title: The Lancet Regional Health - Western Pacific

title: The burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance in the WHO Western Pacific Region 1990–2021: a cross-country systematic analysis with forecasts to 2050
abstract: Background Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is one of the most significant challenges to global health. Although reports from the WHO Western Pacific Region (WPR) increasingly recognise the implications of AMR, precise estimates of the problem's extent remain limited. We present a comprehensive time-trend analysis of AMR burden in the WPR between 1990 and 2021, with forecasts to 2050. Methods Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2021 methods, we estimated deaths and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) attributable to and associated with AMR across 11 infectious syndromes, 22 bacterial pathogens, and 84 pathogen–drug combinations for the WPR and its constituent countries. Data were drawn from mortality registries, surveillance platforms, hospital records, and systematic reviews. The modelling framework comprised five key components: estimation of deaths in which infection had a role, the proportion of infectious deaths attributable to specific syndromes, allocation of syndrome-specific deaths to individual pathogens, the percentage of a given pathogen resistant to an antimicrobial drug of interest, and quantification of the excess mortality risk or prolonged infection duration associated with resistance. Burden was then estimated under two counterfactual scenarios: AMR-attributable (resistant infections replaced by susceptible ones) and AMR-associated (infections prevented altogether). Country-level estimates and forecasts to 2050 were generated using predictive statistical models, with uncertainty reported as 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Findings In 2021, we estimated 1,150,000 deaths (95% UI 1,000,000–1,290,000) associated with bacterial AMR and 248,000 deaths (215,000–281,000) attributable to bacterial AMR across 32 WPR locations. Between 1990 and 2021, deaths in children under 5 dropped by 87.3%, while deaths in adults 70 and older rose by 88.9%. Staphylococcus aureus , Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli accounted for over 50% of AMR deaths. The Solomon Islands and Kiribati had the highest age-standardised mortality rates; New Zealand had the lowest burden in 2021. By 2050, associated and attributable deaths could reach 1,840,000 (1,460,000–2,230,000) and 402,000 (322,000–480,000), respectively. Interpretation The WPR contributes substantially to global AMR burden, with considerable fatal and non-fatal impact from key resistant pathogens. Despite data limitations, these estimates support informed decision-making regarding resource allocation and funding—emphasising the need for collaborative, multi-sectoral action against AMR. Funding Wellcome Trust, and the UK Department of Health and Social Care using aid funding managed by the Fleming Fund.

title: Spatiotemporal trajectories of antimicrobial resistance in bloodstream infections in China: a nationwide longitudinal surveillance study from 2014 to 2023
abstract: Background Bloodstream infections (BSIs) impose a substantial global burden, increasingly complicated by antimicrobial resistance (AMR). We aimed to characterise decade-long trends in BSI pathogens and major resistance phenotypes across mainland China. Methods We analysed BSI surveillance data from 72 hospitals across 22 provinces in the Bacterial Resistant Investigation Collaborative System (BRICS) between 2014 and 2023. Isolates were transferred to a central reference laboratory for species identification and standardised antimicrobial susceptibility testing, with raw minimum inhibitory concentration values retrospectively reinterpreted using 2025 CLSI guidelines. Fourteen continuously participating hospitals formed a sentinel cohort. Findings Among 76,211 non-duplicate BSI isolates, Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae predominated, with K. pneumoniae increasing by 0.91 percentage points annually (95% CI 0.59–1.23; p < 0.001). Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing E. coli decreased from 61.5% to 47.4%, MRSA from 39.0% to 26.2%, and ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae from 30.5% to 21.5% (all p < 0.001). Conversely, carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae increased from 7.0% to 14.9%, peaking at 22.5% in 2018, with marked spatial heterogeneity. CRAB remained persistently high (55.2–64.3%). Resistance proportions were higher in intensive care units, older patients and male patients for several phenotypes. Interpretation Major resistance phenotypes declined during a decade of nationwide antimicrobial stewardship, while the contribution of K. pneumoniae to BSIs increased and carbapenem resistance remained a major challenge. Future AMR strategies should integrate antimicrobial stewardship with targeted infection prevention, outbreak control, and genomic surveillance. Funding This study was supported by Prevention and Control of Emerging and Major Infectious Diseases-National Science and technology Major Project (2025ZD01903301), National Key R&D Program of China (2024YFC2311304) and Research Project of Jinan Microecological Biomedicine Shandong Laboratory (JNL-2025004B).

title: Age-stratified health impacts of climate change on older adults in the Western Pacific Region: a scoping review
abstract: While research on the health impacts of climate change is growing, studies integrating these effects across finer age strata within older adult populations, such as distinguishing young-old from old-old adults remain scarce, particularly in the Western Pacific region. This scoping review synthesizes 119 cases extracted from 100 peer-reviewed studies published from 2016 to 2025, identified via systematic searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase using keyword clusters for older adults, climate change, and the Western Pacific. Most cases (n = 61, 51%) examined heat, followed by extreme cold (n = 31, 26%), air pollution (n = 11, 9%), with geographic concentration in mainland China (n = 84, 71%); old-old adults generally showed greater vulnerability than young-old adults. These findings suggest heterogeneity in climate impacts among older adults, indicating that a one-size-fits-all approach may be insufficient and that finer age stratifications could help inform policies better tailored to old-old adults.

title: Decentralised rare disease care for children living in remote areas: the Pilbara Hub Rare Care model in Western Australia
abstract: Children with Rare Diseases (RD) in rural and remote Australia experience profound inequities in access to coordinated multidisciplinary care.1,2 In the Pilbara region of Western Australia (WA), a vast region spanning over 500,000 square kilometres and located over 1500 km from tertiary paediatric services, children with RD face barrier to diagnosis, specialist review and continuity of care. An estimated 2000 children in the Pilbara are living with RD but service delivery remains constrained by workforce shortages, fragmented care pathways and a dependence on metropolitan models of care with travel required for necessary care.

title: Adult remaining life expectancy among Hong Kong-born and Mainland China/Macao/Taiwan-born residents in Hong Kong
abstract: Background Hong Kong (HK) has among the world's highest life expectancy and a long history of immigration from Mainland China/Macao/Taiwan (MMT). Evidence remains limited on how differences between birthplace groups (HK-born vs. MMT-born) in longevity vary across ages and over time, how adult remaining life expectancy varies by length of stay (LOS) in Hong Kong within MMT-born residents, and which ages and causes of death account for observed gaps. Methods Using death registration and population denominators from the Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department (C&SD), we constructed sex- and birthplace-specific single-age-period life tables for 2006, 2011, 2016, and 2021, and estimated adult remaining life expectancy at age 15 (e 15 ). We used Arriaga decomposition to quantify age- and cause-specific contributions to birthplace group differences in e 15 . Within MMT-born residents, we repeated the analysis by comparing LOS <10 years with LOS ≥10 years. Findings Across all study years and for both sexes, e 15 was higher among Hong Kong-born than MMT-born residents. Among females, the birthplace-group gap widened from 2.6 years in 2006 (72.2 years [95% CI 71.9–72.5] vs. 69.6 [95% CI 69.4–69.7]) to 3.3 years in 2011, before narrowing to 1.3 years in 2021 (72.8 [95% CI 72.6–73.0] vs. 71.5 [95% CI 71.3–71.7]). Among males, the gap widened from 3.4 years in 2006 (67.4 [95% CI 67.0–67.8] vs. 64.0 [95% CI 63.7–64.2]) to 4.8 years in 2016, before narrowing to 2.2 years in 2021 (68.7 [95% CI 68.5–68.8] vs. 66.5 [95% CI 66.3–66.7]). Among MMT-born females and males, shorter LOS was associated with higher e 15 than longer LOS in 2011 and 2016. In 2021, the female difference (shorter minus longer LOS) was 2.61 years (95% CI 0.88–4.53) with the 10-year cutoff, but −0.82 years (95% CI −2.27 to 1.07) with the 7-year cutoff. The corresponding male differences were −3.07 years (95% CI −4.27 to −1.57) and −7.04 years (95% CI −8.45 to −5.24), respectively. Age and cause decomposition showed that the birthplace gap was driven mainly by later-life mortality at ages 65–84 and 85+, and by pneumonia and cancers. Interpretation The observed adult survival advantage of Hong Kong-born over MMT-born residents persisted and was concentrated in later-life mortality, particularly from pneumonia and cancers. Although these descriptive differences should not be interpreted as causal effects of birthplace or LOS, the findings highlight potential priorities for migration-sensitive healthy ageing and mortality surveillance that accounts for place of birth, LOS, and cross-boundary mobility. Funding Daniel and Mayce Yu Medical Development Fund (No. 200010837), and Australian Research Council (ARC DP210100401). The funders had no role in study design, data collection, data analysis, data interpretation, writing of the report, or the decision to submit the paper for publication.
